answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity must accumulate a public history of completed tasks tied to fixed hardware keys and timestamps; new identities start blank. To transact, an agent must wander through a probation period of real, externally verified jobs before gaining standing. Duplicates cannot borrow history, so each fake identity pays the full onboarding cost separately—compute, latency, and lost parallel capacity. The ledger makes mass duplication visible at the orchard of records and at the wharf where jobs queue, since fresh keys flood intake without matching output.
